stem:
Identify nuclear fusion reaction

a. \(^{1}_{1}\mathrm{H} + {}^{1}_{1}\mathrm{H} \longrightarrow {}^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H} + {}^{0}_{1}\mathrm{e}\)

b. \(^{2}_{1}\mathrm{H} + {}^{1}_{1}\mathrm{H} \longrightarrow {}^{3}_{2}\mathrm{He}\)

c. \(^{3}_{1}\mathrm{H} + {}^{1}_{1}\mathrm{H} \longrightarrow {}^{3}_{1}\mathrm{H} + {}^{1}_{1}\mathrm{p}\)

The missing particle from the nuclear reaction is

\(^{27}_{13}\mathrm{Al} + {}^{4}_{2}\mathrm{He} \longrightarrow\ ? + {}^{1}_{0}\mathrm{n}\)
solution: [Textbook misprint: alternative (d) is printed as \(_{14}\mathrm{Si}\), with an atomic number but no mass number. It is wrong either way, since balancing the reaction requires \(Z = 15\), but as printed it cannot even be tested against the mass-number balance.]

stem: \(^{60}_{27}\mathrm{CO}\) decays with half-life of 5.27 years to produce \(^{60}_{28}\mathrm{Ni}\). What is the decay constant for such radioactive disintegration?
solution: [Textbook misprint: the parent nuclide is printed as \(^{60}_{27}\mathrm{CO}\), with a capital O. The element of atomic number 27 is cobalt, whose symbol is Co; CO is carbon monoxide. The nuclide meant is \(^{60}_{27}\mathrm{Co}\), which the chapter itself lists in Table 13.4 (b) with a half life of 5.3 years.]
